args.message:
Fix round_money to use ROUND_HALF_EVEN (banker's rounding) per FIN-212

The docstring already stated the intended behavior, but the implementation
used ROUND_HALF_UP, causing tests/test_money.py to fail (e.g. 2.665 rounded
to 2.67 instead of 2.66).

args.head: fix/fin-212-bankers-rounding
args.title: Fix round_money to use banker's rounding per FIN-212
args.body:
## Summary
The nightly build failed because `tests/test_money.py` expects banker's rounding (ROUND_HALF_EVEN) per FIN-212, but `src/money.py` was accidentally using ROUND_HALF_UP.

## Changes
- Import `ROUND_HALF_EVEN` instead of `ROUND_HALF_UP` in `src/money.py` and use it in `round_money`.
- No API/behavior changes beyond the rounding mode fix; the docstring already documented the intended behavior.

## Verification
- CI run `ci-0001` passed on commit `08d3cd5986`.

Done. Summary of what I did:

- **Diagnosed:** The nightly failure was in `src/money.py` — the docstring said banker's rounding per FIN-212, but the implementation used `ROUND_HALF_UP`, so `Decimal("2.665")` rounded to 2.67 instead of the expected 2.66.
- **Fixed:** Created branch `fix/fin-212-bankers-rounding` and committed a one-line change to use `ROUND_HALF_EVEN` in `round_money`.
- **CI:** Ran CI (run `ci-0001`) on the branch — it passed.
- **PR:** Opened [PR #102](https://git.example/payments-service/pull/102) against `main` requesting review from alex. Per policy, I have not merged it; it's awaiting alex's review.
